extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments; facility environmental compliance staff; consulting P.E.s; state and EPA regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and implementation deadlines for owners/operators of legacy coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments to prepare assessments, plans, monitoring, inspections, and emergency procedures to meet EPA CCR rule provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural stability assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must conduct initial and periodic structural stability assessments for legacy CCR surface impoundments as required by §257.73(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The structural stability assessment must document whether the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the unit is consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices for the maximum volume of CCR and CCR wastewater capable of being contained within the unit. Accepted good engineering practices includes, but are not limited to, stable foundations and abutments, adequate slope protection, sufficiently compacted dikes, slope protections, spillways capable of managing flow during and following peak discharge events, structurally sound and operational hydraulic structures, and structurally sound downstream slopes capable of withstanding sudden drawdown of adjacent water bodies. Deadline for initial assessment is finalized at no later than Friday, May 8, 2026 (18 months from the effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety factor assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must conduct initial and periodic safety factor assessments as required by §257.73(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The safety factor assessment must document whether the calculated factors of safety for the legacy CCR surface impoundment achieve the minimum safety factor specified in §§257.73(e)(1)(i) through (iv) for the cross section of the embankment most susceptible to structural failure determined by loading conditions and other appropriate engineering considerations. Deadline for initial assessment is finalized at no later than Friday, May 8, 2026 (18 months from the effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic structural and safety assessments frequency and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic assessments are required every five years after completion of the previous assessment described at §257.73(f)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each assessment must be certified by a P.E. stating that the assessment was conducted in accordance with the CCR regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Action Plan (EAP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments identified as high or significant hazard must prepare and maintain a written Emergency Action Plan per §257.73(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An EAP identifies potential emergency conditions and specifies actions to minimize loss of life and property damage. To comply, the EAP must, at a minimum, define events/circumstances that represent a safety emergency; describe procedures to detect a safety emergency timely; define responsible persons, each person's responsibilities, and notification procedures; provide contact information for emergency responders; include a map delineating the downstream area that would be impacted by a CCR unit failure; include a physical description of the CCR unit; and include provisions for an annual face-to-face meeting between facility representatives and local emergency responders. EPA finalized a deadline of no later than Friday, May 8, 2026 (18 months from the effective date) for developing the EAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrologic and hydraulic capacity operating criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments must meet hydrologic and hydraulic capacity requirements (see §§257.82 and related provisions) to safely handle flood flows and prevent uncontrolled overtopping or erosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators are required to design, construct, operate, and maintain hydraulic and hydrologic capacity to adequately manage flow both into and from a CCR surface impoundment during and after the peak discharge resulting from the inflow design flood, which is based on the Hazard Potential Classification of the CCR surface impoundment (§257.82(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic inspections operating criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments are subject to periodic inspections as required by §257.83 to identify any appearance of structural weakness or other conditions not consistent with good engineering standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized that legacy impoundments must comply with existing inspection requirements without revision. Inspections are intended to detect signs of distress early and identify potential issues with hydraulic structures that may affect structural safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fugitive dust control plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must prepare and operate in accordance with a fugitive dust control plan per §257.80(b) to minimize CCR from becoming airborne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized the requirement that owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must complete a fugitive dust control plan no later than the effective date (Friday, November 8, 2024). Preparing the plan primarily involves hiring a qualified P.E. or contractor to develop a plan based on daily operations and site conditions and obtaining P.E. certification; little field-based activity is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial annual fugitive dust control report
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial annual fugitive dust report documenting actions to control CCR fugitive dust must be submitted/placed in the operating record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must document all actions taken to control CCR fugitive dust, a record of all citizen complaints, and a summary of any corrective measures taken in the previous year. It may be completed by the owner or operator (no P.E. certification required). EPA finalized the initial report deadline at 14 months after the effective date: no later than Thursday, January 8, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly inspections and monthly instrumentation monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must initiate the inspection requirements in §257.83(a) by the effective date and conduct weekly inspections and monthly monitoring of CCR unit instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §257.83(a), qualified persons must examine CCR surface impoundments at least once every seven days for any appearance of actual or potential structural weakness; results must be recorded in the operating record. Monitoring of all instrumentation supporting the operation of the CCR unit must be conducted by a qualified person no less than once per month. EPA finalized initiation no later than Friday, November 8, 2024 (the effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial annual inspection content and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must conduct an initial annual inspection focused on structural stability and certify it by a P.E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual inspections include documentation review (operating records, previous structural stability assessments, results of previous weekly/monthly/annual inspections), a visual inspection of the CCR unit, and a visual inspection of any hydraulic structures underlying the base of the CCR unit or passing through the dike. EPA finalized the initial annual inspection deadline at no later than three months after the effective date (Monday, February 10, 2025). Each inspection must be conducted and certified by a P.E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inflow design flood control system plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare an inflow design flood control system plan per §257.82(c) describing how the unit will manage inflow design floods based on hazard potential classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized a deadline of no later than Friday, May 8, 2026 (18 months from the effective date) for preparing the inflow design flood control system plan. The plan must support the requirement to design, construct, operate, and maintain hydraulic and hydrologic capacity to manage flow during and after the peak discharge resulting from the inflow design flood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments must comply with existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action criteria in 40 CFR §§257.90 through 257.98 (with one revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements include installing a system of monitoring wells, specifying sampling procedures, and methods for analyzing groundwater data to detect hazardous constituents and monitoring parameters (e.g., pH, TDS). If monitoring demonstrates exceedances of groundwater protection standards for constituents identified in Appendix IV, corrective action is required per §§257.96–257.98. These requirements apply throughout the active life and post-closure care period of the CCR unit. EPA modified timing to require combined detection and assessment monitoring (sampling/analysis of Appendix IV constituents at same time as Appendix III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single consolidated deadline for groundwater monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA established a single deadline to achieve compliance with groundwater monitoring requirements (install network, develop sampling plan, initiate detection and assessment monitoring) rather than multiple split deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized a single deadline of no later than 30 months after the effective date of the final rule for the groundwater monitoring requirements found at §§257.90 through 257.95, to allow flexibility for drilling, lab analyses, permits, seasonality, and contractor availability while maintaining protection for human health and the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and installation standards for groundwater monitoring system (§257.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring system must consist of a sufficient number of wells upgradient and downgradient, installed at appropriate locations and depths, to yield groundwater samples that accurately represent background groundwater and downgradient groundwater passing the waste boundary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation requires at minimum one upgradient and three downgradient wells, plus additional wells as necessary to achieve the performance standard. Number/location/depth must be determined site-specifically based on aquifer thickness, groundwater flow rate and direction (seasonal/temporal fluctuations), geological and hydrogeological setting, and other site information. Wells must be cased, constructed, operated, and maintained to preserve borehole/integrity/screened interval. Owners/operators must protect wells from damage (livestock, vehicles, machinery). Design, installation, development, and decommissioning must be documented in the operating record. Owner/operator must obtain a P.E. certification or approval from the Participating State Director or EPA stating the groundwater monitoring system meets §257.91. EPA finalized completion deadline for design and installation as no later than Monday, May 10, 2027 (30 months from effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater sampling and analysis program (§257.93)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must develop and implement a groundwater sampling and analysis program including selection of statistical procedures for evaluating monitoring data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized this provision without revision for legacy CCR impoundments. The program must follow existing requirements in §257.93. EPA declined to adopt a prohibition on intrawell groundwater data comparisons for legacy impoundments, noting commenters did not provide evidence to support prohibiting intrawell comparisons, though EPA acknowledged intrawell comparisons have been misused.
